text:
morgan: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — a few process Qs about releases, oncall handoffs, and SLAs. Tagging @alexa @sam for ops answers. TL;DR: want clarity on cadence and who's responsible for last-minute rollbacks.

alexa: Thanks — short answers: 

alexa: ```
release cadence: biweekly (Wed 22:00 UTC)
patch release: ad-hoc for sev>=2
rollback owner: oncall primary -> if unavailable, release lead
postmortem: required for sev1/2 within 72h
```

sam: We updated the oncall handoff doc; main changes: explicit handoff checklist, central runbook links, and a `--skip-tests-when=emergency` flag in the release job for emergency patches. ping @devops-bot to show deploy job example.

devops-bot: deploy-job: updated config: `--skip-tests-when=emergency` (use sparingly) — see /infra/ci-pipeline#release-job

priya: Quick q: what's the SLA difference for Dedicated customers vs Hosted? Need wording for customer comms.

morgan: Good question. Short answer:
- Hosted: operational reporting and Uptime dashboards, no financial credits.
- Dedicated: 99.9% monthly uptime with service credits for violations.
- Private: SLA is contract-specific (legal + account teams).
Ops will draft the formal wording by EOD Friday.

alexa: :thumbsup: will draft and post to #support and product-legal.

sam: Also: quality bar reminder — any model change must pass perf/regression evals in CI and a 1% canary before full rollout. We'll add that to the release checklist.

priya: Thanks — one last ask: can we publish the release calendar to the org calendar so teams can plan?

morgan: Yes, calendar invite will go out today. Closing this thread — please file concrete follow-ups in the release-playbook doc or ping me directly.
